accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE A level Mathematics subject content (statistical distributions: understand and use the binomial distribution as a model, calculate probabilities, and judge when it is suitable), the Edexcel, AQA and OCR statistics specifications (conditions: fixed n, two outcomes, independent trials, constant p) and the College Board AP Statistics course description (BINS and the 10% condition for sampling without replacement). The lab band uses the exact hypergeometric extremes for 20 draws at 10% faulty.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: 'until' contexts with no fixed n, multi-outcome counts such as a die score, p taken as the failure probability (define step traps and practice p2), ignoring sampling without replacement from a small population (bag step, population slider), assuming independence for weather spells, and swapping n and p in B(n, p).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbfit is built on four condition lamps judged per context, a bag with live P(red) under and without replacement, a log slider for population size against a p band, and an n-line with p tiles to define X ~ B(n, p). flagpdist builds a dice distribution grid, flagperm arranges objects, and flagpasc builds rows of coefficients; none of them test model conditions.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step checks one idea: all four conditions, why replacement keeps p constant, when a large population makes without replacement close to binomial, finding the single broken condition, and stating the model in context with success defined.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions before acting: what happens to P(red) after a red is kept out, and whether a larger population makes the binomial fit better or worse.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five challenge questions, each wrong choice tagged to a specific misconception with a targeted explanation (no fixed n, more than two outcomes, dependence, small population, p for the wrong outcome).

readability.evidence: Learner kid text FK 2.2 and adult text FK 8.2, both inside the learner limits; key terms are defined on first use.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a condition, an example or a named mistake; no stock phrases.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 and desktop; lamps, tiles and the slider stack in one column on narrow screens with 44 px or larger targets, and drags work by touch.

accessibility.evidence: axe passes in light and dark themes; all colours come from the theme kit, the canvas has an aria-label, and every drag has a button or key alternative.
